prompt: Complete Applier: applyTwice applies a UnaryOperator to a starting value two times, and countMatching counts array entries accepted by an IntPredicate.
explanation: Functional interface parameters let callers pass behavior as data: applyTwice never knows what op does, it just calls apply twice, and countMatching delegates each accept-or-reject decision to p.test. IntPredicate is the primitive specialization of Predicate<Integer>, so testing int values involves no boxing. The tests supply different lambdas to exercise the same two methods.
hints: UnaryOperator<Integer> has an apply method -- call it with start, then call it again with that first result.
IntPredicate's test method returns a boolean; count how many array entries make it true.
A simple for-each loop over values with a counter variable is all countMatching needs.
